summary: Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Dagpo Rinpoche studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche. He taught David Seyfort Ruegg, Anne-Marie Blondeau, Thoupten Phuntshog, and Marie-Stella Boussemart.
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Daichi Tado held part-time lecturer posts attested in 2020 at both Waseda University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Daiei Kaneko worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University (~1901–1904) under Manshi Kiyozawa (~1901–1903), later teaching at Otani University (~1911–1951) and Toyo University, and founding Koho Gakuen.

Daiju Sasaki specializes in Buddhist studies, having studied at Taisho University. In 2015, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and a full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpōin.

Daijō Tokiwa worked in Buddhist studies and sinology, studying at the University of Tokyo (1895–1898) under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo (1925–1931) and Toyo University (1931).

In Buddhist studies, Dainin Katagiri trained at Eihei-ji (~1946–1953) under teachers including Eko Hashimoto, and graduated from Komazawa University (~1953–1957). He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and as interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center (1984–1985).

Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki studied at the University of Tokyo under Kosen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held professorships at Otani University (1921–1960) and Columbia University (1952–1957).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology, Daishun Ueyama studied under Akira Fujieda. He served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (~1969–1974) and later as president in 1983.

Daito Shimaji worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology after studying at Ryukoku and Toyo Universities. He taught at Toyo University (~1903–1927), lectured on Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo (1923), and taught at Komazawa and Rissho.

Dale S. Wright specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann. He served as Gamble Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College (~1980–2017).

Dalsukh Malvania worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi (~1930–1940). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1957) and served as Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (~1957–1975).
Damchö Gyatso studied under Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, Penor Rinpoche, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was active in Tibetology and linguistics, having studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, earning degrees from Lancaster University and the University of Oxford (D.Phil.). He served at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1986–2012), where he became Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics.

Kosambi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After graduating from Harvard under George David Birkhoff, he held mathematics professorships at Fergusson College (1932) and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962), later becoming Scientist Emeritus at CSIR (1964).

Dan Arnold specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago and taught as Assistant Professor of Philosophy of Religion at the University of Chicago Divinity School (2004–2011) and McGill University (2003–2004).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning a Ph.D. from Temple University under scholars including Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Florida State University, University of Georgia, and Harvard University (2005).

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Indiana University (~1983–1991) under Elliot Sperling, later holding posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters (~1995–1996) and Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1996).

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who earned his PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and a Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He became Professor of Philosophy at Copenhagen (2002) and Professor of Philosophy at Oxford (2018–2021).
